s1.syndrome_frame: Painful, crusted, erythematous skin lesion on the chest with a 2-week history
salient_findings: Large, crusted, erythematous plaque on the right chest
Painful area on the right lateral chest
key_facts: Female patient in her 50s
2-week history of a painful area on the right lateral chest
Taking prednisone, 10 mg, daily
Previous treatments included methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, glycopyrrolate, oral antibiotics, topical corticosteroids, topical calcineurin inhibitors, and topical antibiotics
Biopsy was previously performed
Laboratory values within normal limits for intact parathyroid hormone, ionized calcium, and phosphorus

shortlist.label: Eczematous dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: previous treatments included topical corticosteroids and history of painful skin lesion

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: large, crusted, erythematous plaque and previous biopsy

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: painful skin lesion with crusting and erythema

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: skin lesion with erythema and crusting, and patient taking prednisone

raw.rationale: The patient's history of a painful, crusted, erythematous plaque, along with a history of unsuccessful treatments with various medications, is consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum, a condition known for its challenging treatment and potential for significant tissue damage.

rejected.label: Eczematous dermatitis
rejected.why: While eczematous dermatitis can present with erythematous plaques, the patient's lack of response to topical corticosteroids and other treatments makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: There is no specific mention of lymphoma-like symptoms or biopsy results that would strongly suggest cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The description of the lesion as a crusted, erythematous plaque does not strongly suggest squamous cell carcinoma, which typically presents as a more defined, possibly ulcerated nodule or plaque.

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation lacks the characteristic skin manifestations and muscle weakness typically associated with dermatomyositis.
